method: Viewed original and target full size, 2x enlarged crops of the top-left cell group (target) and matching original region, a seam crop of the original right block, and both downscaled to 360 px wide side by side (approximate phone use size). Sampled mean RGB on a top face and a front face in each image.

measuredSamples.note: Approximate means over small patches; for calibration of direction only, not exact targets.

sourceAssessment.reads: Correct approved blocking: slabs, heights, rounded exposed corners, flush cell joins, low rubble. Clearly paler than the blue bedrock and the seabed.
weaknesses: Material is flat untextured cream plastic: tops nearly white and desaturated (approx 246,233,198), no per-slab tone variation, no pores, cracks or chips. Reads as tiles/bricks or butter, not breakable stone.
Front (south) faces are one uniform khaki gradient; the top-to-front value step is modest and the side has no strata, so at phone size the blocks read as soft paper boxes.
Top chamfer band renders as a pale greyish rim lighter and cooler than the top itself, giving a plastic/bevelled-button look instead of a warm caught highlight.
Some interior slab grooves show slivers of seabed blue, and some junctions show small dark brown wedges where a lower slab peeks out. Grooves read as gaps or holes rather than thin soft shadow lines.
Faint diagonal shading lines are visible on some large tops at full size (likely triangulation/normal interpolation on n-gon tops); minor but should not survive into the surfaced version.
Rubble is pale cream like the tops with a flat tan side: acceptable shape, but no material continuity cues with the stone beyond colour.

takes: Warmer, more saturated limestone: peach-cream tops (approx 253,221,168) and a clearly deeper warm tan front (approx 181,131,80). Larger top/front value contrast; the blocks read as solid stone volumes.
Per-slab tone variation on tops (some warmer, some paler) without becoming noisy.
Front faces carry soft horizontal strata bands, darkening slightly toward the seabed; strata of horizontally adjacent pieces sit at matching heights.
Fine hairline cracks (a few per slab, not every slab), sparse small round pores, and occasional small chipped corners on top edges. These are the main 'breakable' cue.
Chamfered top edge catches a soft warm highlight, not a grey band.
Grooves between slabs read as narrow warm shadow lines; no seabed blue shows inside the reef.
Rubble shares the limestone colours: lit tops, shaded tan sides.
driftNotToCopy: Some chips in the target bite visibly into the front/top outline and rounded corners (e.g. large wedge chips on front edges); at ground level the outline is locked to <=0.03 cell inward.
Exact slab edges, corner radii and some block outlines drift a few pixels from registration; geometry must come from the recipe, not the image.
Cracks that run from the top down the full front face to the ground are fine as shader/shallow detail but must not change the silhouette.
Imagegen softness/blur and slightly uneven crack density between cells; the native result should have consistent density everywhere.
The target's top tone is close to the edge of 'too orange'; the pale/warm read versus the blue bedrock must be kept, so do not push saturation further than the target.

phoneSizeFindings: At 360 px wide the single biggest perceptual difference is colour/value: warm peach tops over a distinctly darker warm tan front versus the original's near-white over khaki. This alone moves the read from 'cream tiles' to 'sandstone/limestone blocks'.
Second: front strata bands remain visible at phone size and give the stone identity; pores mostly vanish; the larger cracks and chips remain faintly visible as texture.
Third: grooves as warm dark lines (instead of blue slits or bright rims) make each cell read as a solid mass that can be smashed.
Fine pores and hairline cracks are secondary at use size: they matter at 2x but must not create speckle or shimmer when downsampled.
priorities: Warm limestone colour/value structure (tops vs fronts, per-slab variation) while staying clearly pale vs bedrock
Seam-safe front strata and tone across all masks
Breakable cues: hairline cracks, small chipped corners, sparse pores, consistent density
Warm soft chamfer highlight replacing the grey rim; grooves as soft warm shadows, no blue slivers or dark wedges
Matching rubble material; no new artifacts (speckle, normal seams, triangulation lines)
